name: Goal Setting & Time Management

objectives.text: Identify a short-term goal and the steps needed to reach it
Use a calendar or planner to record schoolwork, chores, and animal or garden care tasks with their due dates
Distinguish between short-term and long-term goals and give an agricultural example of each
Prioritize a list of tasks by urgency and importance to decide what to do first
Identify common time wasters and procrastination habits and propose a strategy to overcome each
Write a SMART goal for a chapter activity or SAE project
Analyze a one-week time log to compare planned and actual use of time
Identify methods for setting personal improvement goals in an AFNR career area such as SMART goals, training, and professional development
Conduct a self-assessment of personal time management, planning, and prioritizing habits and identify strengths and areas for growth
Identify the requirements for the next FFA degree and set a goal and timeline for earning it
Apply a weekly planning system to balance SAE, chapter, and school responsibilities
Prepare short-term, intermediate, and long-term SMART goals that are consistent with the purpose of an entrepreneurship or placement SAE
Build a production or work timeline for an SAE that accounts for seasonal deadlines such as breeding, planting, harvest, and show or fair entry dates
Evaluate progress toward a personal or SAE goal using record book data and revise the plan based on results
Create a personal leadership development plan with goals and action steps to improve a characteristic such as time management or organization
Develop a goal-based plan of action with a timeline, assigned responsibilities, and evaluation measures for a chapter Program of Activities event
Justify priority decisions among competing commitments to SAE, school, work, family, and church
Develop a multi-year goal plan connecting SAE growth, FFA degree advancement, and education and career pathway

changes: Kept all six existing objectives as real competencies, rewording a few. The grade 6 objective now asks for distinguishing goal types with agricultural examples. The grade 8 objective now asks students to write a SMART goal rather than practice setting one. The grade 11 objective now evaluates progress against SAE record book data. Added the missing time management skills: planner use, prioritizing by urgency and importance, overcoming time wasters, and analyzing a time log. Added high school competencies tied to the AFNR standards: goal-setting methods, a self-assessment of planning habits, FFA degree goal setting, tiered SMART goals for an SAE enterprise, seasonal SAE timelines, a personal leadership development plan, Program of Activities action planning, and justifying priorities among competing commitments. Left team facilitation and character content to the sibling sub-topics. Mapped standards only where an objective directly teaches one.
